source.archive: Cui, Li, and Zhou OSF replication archive
source.prompt_locator: prompt.xlsx rows with Journal=JEP, Essay=8, Study=4
source.source_article: Burgmer, Forstmann, and Stavrova (2019), Ideas are cheap: When and why adults value labor over ideas
authorized_normalizations: Removed the archive's generic LLM wrapper and reason-generation request.
Restored the source construct in the negative arm: blame for the negative outcome rather than praise for a positive outcome.
Used arm-specific item text so each participant sees only praise or blame wording for the assigned outcome.
Kept Jesse and Alex target ratings separate and retained effort and comprehension items as secondary.

design.primary_estimand: [E(Alex - Jesse praise|positive outcome)] - [E(Alex - Jesse blame|negative outcome)]

population.simulation_target: Adult evaluating credit and blame for a jointly produced meal

materials.participant_role: Act as one adult participant judging the two contributors described below. Respond for yourself, do not predict the average person, and do not analyze the experiment.
materials.common_scenario: Two friends, Jesse and Alex, want to surprise a mutual friend, Sam, with a home-cooked meal. Jesse thinks of a recipe for the meal. Alex then cooks the meal.

positive_outcome.label: Positive meal outcome
positive_outcome.stimulus: Sam arrives, tries the meal, really likes the food, finishes the whole dish, and asks for more.

negative_outcome.label: Negative meal outcome
negative_outcome.stimulus: Sam arrives, tries the meal, does not like the food at all, does not finish the dish, and would never ask for more.

materials.response_instruction: Return only integer item responses in the required JSON structure. Use the 1-to-7 or 1-to-2 bounds shown for each item.

items.text: How much outcome-appropriate evaluation does Jesse deserve?

text_by_arm.positive_outcome: How much praise does Jesse deserve for the positive outcome?
text_by_arm.negative_outcome: How much blame does Jesse deserve for the negative outcome?

items.text: How much outcome-appropriate evaluation does Alex deserve?

text_by_arm.positive_outcome: How much praise does Alex deserve for the positive outcome?
text_by_arm.negative_outcome: How much blame does Alex deserve for the negative outcome?

items.text: Who invested more effort? Use 1 for definitely Jesse and 7 for definitely Alex.
Who spent more time? Use 1 for definitely Jesse and 7 for definitely Alex.
Who really exerted themself? Use 1 for definitely Jesse and 7 for definitely Alex.
Who had the idea for the recipe? Use 1 for Jesse and 2 for Alex.
Did Sam enjoy the meal? Use 1 for yes and 2 for no.

research_restricted.aligned_hypothesis_text: The Alex-minus-Jesse target difference is more positive for praise after success than for blame after failure.
research_restricted.reversed_hypothesis_text: The Alex-minus-Jesse target difference is more positive for blame after failure than for praise after success.
